mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals tighter monetary conditions, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2 percentage points over one month indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of cases when UNRATE increases by 0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of cases when HOUST increases by 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO declines by 1%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and stagnant payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of cases when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS is stagnant, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weak aggregate demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of cases when both GDPC1 and RSAFS decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) during an economic expansion signals increased corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 25% of cases during economic expansion with strong GDPC1 growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 300 signals increased inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 45% of cases when CPIAUCSL exceeds 300, the hypothesis is rejected.
